newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks set new closing record above 2,500.
newsitem.headline: French stocks set new closing record above 2,500.

text.p: French stocks rallied to historic highs on Thursday, propelling the blue-chip CAC-40 index above 2,500 points for the first time, after the Bank of France trimmed its leading intervention rate.

The CAC-40 index finished up 38.05 points, or 1.54 percent, at 2,503.06, boosted by a 15.53 percent surge in shares of electrical engineering group Alcatel Alsthom, which said it expected to show net income of 2.5 billion francs for 1996. Analysts were expecting a profit closer to 1.4 billion.
Traders said the bourse was underpinned by continuing gains on Wall Street.
The CAC-40 January futures contract closed 30.50 points higher at 2,495.50.
Volume was a heavy 10.65 billion francs, including 8.24 billion in the CAC-40 issues.
Within the first month of the year, the CAC index has pushed past the expectations of most market operators who estimated in December that it would peak this year at around 2,450 points.
"They've just gone crazy," said one trader.
Alcatel shares led the rally, finishing up 70 francs at 523, after the market applauded its rebound from a 1995 loss of 25.6 billion francs due to massive restructuring charges.
Traders said Alcatel's performance stirred interest in lagging cyclical stocks.

* PSA Peugeot Citroen shares, which have recently underperformed both the bourse and shares in rival Renault, closed up 5.28 percent at 598 francs. "Peugeot's catching up," one analyst said. Traders said Natwest Sellier had put out a buy on the stock. The firm declined comment.

* Michelin hit a new year high of 322 francs before closing at 320.50, up 3.29 percent, after a series of positive recommendations by investment firms. The group this week denied talk it may be planning a capital increase.
Finance Director Eric Bourdais de Charbonniere told reporters this week that the tyremaker's strategy remained to keep reducing debt using cashflow.

* Shares in Rhone-Poulenc slipped 0.39 percent to 179.80 francs. The chemicals company said net income rose 28 percent in 1996 to 2.74 billion francs. Chairman Rene Fourtou said the improvement was encouraging, but the result remained "insufficient for a company of our size".
* LVMH shares slipped 0.82 percent to 1,450 francs prior to releasing its 1996 sales. It reported a 4.6 percent rise in 1996 sales after the market's close.
It said it expected the recent acquisition of DFS to have a dilutive effect in 1997, with lower earnings per share, but expects higher sales and profits before the impact of the acquisition.
* Saint-Gobain closed up 4.68 percent at 850 francs ahead of its results. After the close, it reported a rise in net attributable profit to 4.32 billion francs from 4.21 billion.
* Accor was buoyed 2.98 percent to 726 francs by speculation of a bid by Bass Plc, triggered in turn by Hilton Corp's offer for ITT Corp. Accor declined comment.
